document: GridSignal Simulator — Calculation and Parameter Reference v0.1
parent_spec: GridSignal Forecast Engine Functional Specification v2.5
usage_note: Load this file at runtime. Do not hard-code any value below into application code. Generate the settings modal from the 'ui' block of each entry so the modal cannot drift from the documented ranges.

provenance_classes.MEASURED: Observed at an operating site. Currently: none.
provenance_classes.VENDOR_RATING: Manufacturer nameplate figure, not observed draw.
provenance_classes.SPEC_DEFAULT: Value and range both fixed in v2.5.
provenance_classes.ESTIMATE: Value appears in v2.5; no range given. Midpoint or judgement.
provenance_classes.PROPOSED_HERE: Not present in v2.5. Introduced by this document; requires review.
provenance_classes.CONFORMANCE: Constant under acceptance test. Not user-adjustable.

parameter_sets.note: Entries with split=true exist twice at runtime: plant.<id> is simulated physics, engine.<id> is what the forecast believes. They are linked by default; unlinking must be a visible user action. Entries with split=false exist once, engine-side.

adjustable.label: Δt_lead — allocation to full TDP
adjustable.note: A software artifact, not a physical constant. Shrinks as image caching and weight loading improve.

adjustable.label: Δt_thermal — cooling response delay
adjustable.note: Default is the midpoint of the range, not a measurement. Primary candidate for the plant/engine divergence demo.

adjustable.label: τ — cooling rise time constant
adjustable.provenance_detail: Default from v2.5 §8; the 10–40 range is proposed by this document.

adjustable.label: r_asset — turbine ramp rate per unit
adjustable.provenance_detail: Default from v2.5 §7.1; the 0.1–0.5 range is proposed by this document.
adjustable.time_varying_note: The only parameter that may legitimately vary within a run: cold vs warm start, ambient derate, and a discontinuous step on unit trip or additional unit online.

adjustable.label: PUE_base — non-cooling overhead
adjustable.provenance_detail: IT-side overhead only: power conversion, distribution losses, UPS, lighting. Excludes active cooling (§4.1). Range [1.01, 1.10] is consistent with measured IT overhead for gas-turbine-backed edge DCs. Code default wins over the prior catalogue entry of 1.11 (which incorrectly assumed cooling was included).
adjustable.note: Must exclude active cooling. Overlap with α(t) reintroduces the double-count v2.5 §4 exists to resolve.

adjustable.label: BESS state of charge
adjustable.open_item: OI-6 — the derate function f(SOC) on bridging capability has no specified form.

adjustable.label: P_anchor_reserve — grid-forming headroom
adjustable.provenance_detail: v2.5 §7.1.2 requires a conservative fraction and forbids defaulting to zero, but supplies no number. 8% is a placeholder.
adjustable.note: Applies only when the BESS is grid-forming. Grid-connected, the utility is the reference and this term is zero.

adjustable.label: P_renewable — non-dispatchable supply
adjustable.note: Measured/forecast input, never a commanded setpoint. Reduces load; contributes nothing to ramp capability. A step loss carries Δt_lead = 0.

enumerated.label: Hardware profile
enumerated.note: This control IS the kW-per-node control. Selecting generic_fallback must trigger the §5.1 path and the PARAM-15 widening.

enumerated.label: Workload class
enumerated.note: inference additionally requires queue_depth / request_rate per the §10 contract.

enumerated.label: Turbines online
enumerated.note: Integer, never a slider. Aggregate ramp = turbine_count × r_asset. Ramp scales with unit count, not installed MW: 3 × 15 MW gives 3× the step response of 1 × 25 MW. N−1 firm capacity is the binding constraint.

enumerated.label: Grid mode
enumerated.note: Gates PARAM-09. Anchor role is dynamic and must be read from the power management system, not inferred from configuration.

enumerated.label: Operating tier
enumerated.note: Advisory: dashboard warning only. Supervised/Autonomous: hard alert requiring acknowledgment (TC-14).

enumerated.label: Clock discipline
enumerated.note: Third option exercises TC-70: a false precision claim is demoted to the NTP bound.

enumerated.label: Fabric signal tier
enumerated.note: Lower tiers degrade roles, never ingestion (TC-71).

enumerated.label: Scenario
enumerated.note: Loads a complete parameter set. Loading a preset mid-run is a scenario event per INV-7.

locked.reason: Under acceptance test TC-06…TC-09. Display, do not expose. Thresholds are inclusive, not strict.
Adjusting a requirement to pass a test inverts the test.

locked.label: Ambient cooling nominal — ASHRAE 90.4 moderate-climate reference design temperature
locked.provenance_detail: 21 °C is the ASHRAE 90.4-2019 §6.4 reference design ambient for moderate climates and is consistent with ASHRAE TC 9.9 baseline conditions. No site-specific measurement exists yet; this replaces the PROTO-32-AMB placeholder of 19 °C (arbitrary midpoint of the San Diego 14–24 °C range).
locked.note: Temperature at which ambient_alpha_scale() returns 1.0 — no derate applied. Requires commissioning measurement to graduate to MEASURED. Paired with ambient_cooling_scale_per_c.

locked.label: Ambient cooling coefficient — α_max derate per °C from nominal
locked.provenance_detail: 1.5 %/°C is the published mean COP regression slope for air-cooled chillers in the ASHRAE TC 9.9 guidance documents (15–35 °C ambient range). No site measurement exists yet; this replaces the PROTO-32-AMB placeholder of 1.0 %/°C (no prior basis).
locked.note: scale = 1.0 + 0.015 × (T_amb − 21). Clamped to [0.80, 1.20]. At 14 °C → 0.895; at 24 °C → 1.045. Requires commissioning measurement to graduate to MEASURED.

locked.label: Minimum stable load fraction — all turbine units (universal CHOSEN default)
locked.provenance_detail: Phase E §7.1.3.6 / PW-1: 0.40 is the frame-class representative lean-extinction boundary.  Originally applied only to demo-20mw turbine units (7 MW rated; MSL = 2.8 MW per unit, PARAM formerly 'p_min_stable_frac_demo').  Phase E Item 8 propagated the value to all 23 remaining seeded scenarios; Phase E closeout Item 2 reconciled the two catalogue entries (p_min_stable_frac_demo + p_min_stable_frac_all_scenarios → this single authoritative entry keyed to match TurbineConfig.p_min_stable_frac).  No OEM combustion stability measurement on file.  A production deployment must replace this with frame-class-specific data (PROTO-R4).  BessConfig does not carry this field; 0.0 is still a valid per-unit override for units without a combustion floor.
locked.note: MSL = p_min_stable_frac × rated_mw.  demo-20mw example: 0.40 × 7.0 = 2.8 MW per unit; Σ msl (4 online) = 11.2 MW; (5 incl. hot-standby) = 14.0 MW.  sub_msl_surplus_mw > 0 when p_fleet < Σ MSL (TC-95 sub-MSL path; TC-96 sequential-fill).  TurbineConfig.p_min_stable_frac reads this key via _sp.value() at class definition time (Guard D1 clean — no literal).

locked.label: Minimum continuous run time before a controlled stop is accepted
locked.provenance_detail: Phase E Item 8 / §7.1.3.6: 1800 s (30 min) is a representative minimum stable operating period for frame-class gas turbines before a controlled shutdown.  Prevents hot-cold thermal shock and combustor re-ignition churn.  No OEM specification on file; requires frame-class commissioning data to graduate from CHOSEN.  Enforced in command_stop() via R5 guard: stop deferred silently when elapsed < t_min_run_s.
locked.note: R5 enforcement (closeout Item 1 / D-03): command_stop() returns block reason 'r5_min_run_not_elapsed:...' when sim_time − _run_start_s < t_min_run_s and min_run_enabled=True.  The commitment engine threads the reason into CommitmentDecision.blocked_by and retries on the next decommit check.  Set min_run_enabled=False (TurbineConfig default) to disable the guard in unit tests that do not model minimum run-time constraints.

locked.label: Minimum offline interval (cooling/purge) before a restart is accepted
locked.provenance_detail: Phase E Item 8 / §7.1.3.6: 900 s (15 min) is a representative cooling and purge cycle duration for frame-class gas turbines between a controlled stop and the next start.  No OEM specification on file; requires frame-class commissioning data to graduate from CHOSEN.  Enforced in command_start() via R6 guard: start silently dropped when elapsed < t_min_down_s.
locked.note: R6 enforcement (closeout Item 1 / D-03): command_start() returns without transitioning if sim_time − _stop_time_s < t_min_down_s and min_down_enabled=True.  Set min_down_enabled=False (TurbineConfig default) to disable the guard.  TC-203-3 exercises the disabled-cooldown path — min_down_enabled=False is the correct way to express it after the D-03 refactor.

locked.label: BESS anchor reserve — San Diego demo plant site override
locked.provenance_detail: PW-3 / §15: 2.0 MW is an explicit scenario-level override for the San Diego demo-20mw plant's grid-forming BESS (bess-0, 18 MW / 8 MWh). The BessConfig class default is 1.0 MW (PROTO-9).  This override provides 2× the default headroom in both charge and discharge directions to account for the larger inverter rating at this site.  No measured frequency-regulation spec from the design partner; calibration required.
locked.note: Applied in api/routes/scenarios.py demo-20mw BessUnitSpec only. BessConfig.p_anchor_reserve_mw default (1.0 MW) is unchanged so all other scenarios that do not set an explicit override remain unaffected. TC-81 asserts the class default is still 1.0 MW.

locked.label: Cooling-plant sizing margin over α_max × peak IT load
locked.provenance_detail: What the 15% covers AFTER Phase 6 (PUE overhead removed from scope — it is now inside peak_it_load_mw = nodes × kW × PUE_base / 1000): (1) BESS charge overhead — inverter losses ~2–4% appear as additional heat during charging cycles; (2) non-compute IT load — networking switches, PDUs, UPS auxiliary draw ~3–8% of compute rack load; (3) ambient excursion headroom — ambient_alpha_scale raises effective cooling fraction by up to ~4.5% above nominal (3°C × 1.5%/°C per locked ambient_cooling_scale_per_c), which the cooling plant must cover without saturation; (4) cooling-plant efficiency margin — real chillers operate below nameplate at partial load, ~2–5% headroom needed. Sum of remaining jobs: 11.5–21.5%; 1.15 is the CHOSEN midpoint (PROTO-10). CHOSEN — no measured thermal-engineering basis. Calibrate against mechanical-plant commissioning data.
locked.note: rated_cooling_mw = alpha_max × peak_it_load_mw × cooling_margin. Previously hardcoded as _COOLING_MARGIN = 1.15. PUE overhead is no longer a job of this margin (absorbed into peak_it_load_mw in Phase 6). Value 1.15 unchanged; stated rationale corrected in Phase 7.

locked.label: Solar-array rated output as fraction of peak IT load
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — no measured on-site solar resource data. 20-30% of peak IT load is the design range for a representative on-site renewable contribution that keeps P_dispatch_required non-zero (BESS bridging, reserve checks, and §7.1.1 renewable-shortfall scenarios remain exercisable). 25% is the midpoint. See PROTO-7.
locked.note: solar_rated_mw = solar_fraction_of_peak × peak_it_load_mw. Formerly hardcoded as 0.25 in scenario_factory.py:145, :273. Now read through site_parameters.py.

locked.label: BESS anchor reserve — class default
locked.provenance_detail: 1.0 MW is the class default withheld from bridging on the grid-forming BESS unit to maintain frequency-regulation headroom in both charge and discharge directions (§7.1.2). CHOSEN — non-zero per TC-63; no measured frequency-regulation specification from design partner (PROTO-9). The San Diego demo plant overrides this to 2.0 MW via spec-level anchor_reserve_pct.
locked.note: Default for BessConfig.p_anchor_reserve_mw. Scenario-level override via anchor_reserve_pct. See locked entry p_anchor_reserve_mw_san_diego for the San Diego site override.

locked.label: BESS bridging escalation floor
locked.provenance_detail: 15% of aggregate BESS rated MW is a conservative early-warning floor pending site commissioning data.

locked.label: BESS bridging floor anchor multiple
locked.provenance_detail: The operational floor may not be below two times configured grid-forming anchor reserve.

locked.label: Material BESS discharge threshold
locked.provenance_detail: 5% of aggregate nameplate rejects regulation chatter while retaining sensitivity to a sustained bridge.

locked.label: Minimum material BESS discharge
locked.provenance_detail: 1 MW absolute minimum prevents small fleets and telemetry noise from starting the sustained timer.

locked.label: BESS discharge catch-up confirmation
locked.provenance_detail: Six 5-second ticks aligns with commit_confirm_s and rejects transient step-load bridging.

locked.label: Turbine catch-up slope window
locked.provenance_detail: Three 5-second intervals provide a stable observed ramp without consuming the full confirmation window.

locked.label: Turbine catch-up bridge-time margin
locked.provenance_detail: Catch-up must complete within 80% of remaining BESS bridge duration, preserving a 20% timing margin.

locked.label: Commitment trigger — fleet utilisation threshold
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.80 is the midpoint of the 75–85% range used by independent system operators for spinning-reserve dispatch triggers. No measured basis against this fleet class (UC-1). Calibrate against commissioning data.
locked.note: Start the next offline unit when fleet utilisation U = P_demand / Σ rated_SYNCHRONISED ≥ this value, sustained commit_confirm_s seconds. Primary commit trigger. Reserve-floor violation is the secondary (always-binding) trigger.

locked.label: Decommitment trigger — fleet utilisation threshold
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.50 provides a 30-point gap below commit_utilisation (0.80), giving a 300 s decommit hysteresis window time to expire before conditions re-trigger a commit. No measured basis (UC-2). The asymmetry (commit 0.80, decommit 0.50) is normative per §7.1.3.
locked.note: Consider decommitting the last-committed unit only when U ≤ this value, sustained decommit_confirm_s seconds. Must be evaluated together with decommit_post_removal_max and the reserve floor.

locked.label: Decommitment — maximum utilisation after unit removal
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.70 is below commit_utilisation (0.80) so decommitting does not immediately re-trigger a commit. No measured basis (UC-3). The 10-point gap is a tuning parameter; production systems should set it from load-forecast variance.
locked.note: The utilisation that would result from removing the candidate unit (P_demand / Σ rated_remaining) must not exceed this value. Guards against decommitting into an immediately-recommit situation.

locked.label: Commitment confirmation window
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 30 s is short enough to prevent load-shedding during a sustained demand step but long enough to reject a transient spike lasting fewer than six 5-second ticks. No measured basis (UC-1). The 30 s / 300 s asymmetry (commit fast, decommit slow) is normative.
locked.note: Fleet utilisation must exceed commit_utilisation continuously for this many seconds before a commit command is issued. Resets to 0 on any tick where the condition is false.

locked.label: Decommitment confirmation window
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 300 s equals one cold-start time (r_asset 0.2 MW/s × 7 MW ≈ 35 s + startup countdown; round to a commissioning-friendly 5-minute window). Prevents short-cycling a turbine that was just committed. No measured basis (UC-4). Normative asymmetry: 10× commit_confirm_s.
locked.note: All decommit conditions must hold continuously for this many seconds. The long window prevents short-cycling (commit → decommit → commit within one cold-start window).

locked.label: Contingency hot-standby release confirmation window
locked.provenance_detail: Engineering estimate pending validation against turbine trip and reserve-response data. Shorter than ordinary commitment confirmation because the N-1 risk is already present, but long enough to reject a single 5-second telemetry tick.
locked.note: COVERED_WITH_SHED or CANNOT_CARRY must persist continuously for this duration before one hot-standby turbine may be released. Placeholder pending real tuning.

locked.label: Inter-start settle interval
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 60 s is approximately twice the synchronisation time for the default turbine (r_asset 0.2 MW/s × 7 MW ≈ 35 s). Gives the first unit time to settle at a stable setpoint before the commitment engine can issue a second start command. No measured basis (UC-1).
locked.note: PendingStartRegister.settled_at() uses this value. The next command_start() may not issue until inter_start_settle_s has elapsed since the previous unit reached SYNCHRONISED.

locked.label: Levelled-off output deadband
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.05 MW is 0.7% of the default 7 MW turbine rated output. Provides numerical tolerance for floating-point convergence of the setpoint tracking loop without masking real load-following errors. No measured basis.
locked.note: A unit is considered levelled-off when |output_mw - setpoint_mw| < levelled_off_epsilon_mw, sustained levelled_off_window_s seconds. levelled_off is a derived predicate, never a TurbineState.

locked.label: Levelled-off confirmation window
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 10 s (two 5-second ticks) is the minimum window to confirm a unit has settled, avoiding false levelled-off detection during transient output oscillation. No measured basis.
locked.note: The levelled-off condition (|output - setpoint| < levelled_off_epsilon_mw) must be sustained this many seconds before the stop sequencer considers the unit ready to begin unloading (Phase E).

locked.reason: Settling dwell from levelled_off True to breaker open (and minimum inter-unit stop spacing under sequential decommit). Must strictly exceed levelled_off_window_s (10 s): if unload_tail_s <= levelled_off_window_s then _levelled_off_sustained is never True and the panel indicator silently absent. CHOSEN — calibrate against OEM breaker and droop-response data before production deployment.

locked.label: Turbine ramp rate
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.2 MW/s is the Section 7.1 MVP default.  No measured basis.  A production deployment must replace this with OEM ramp-rate data for the installed frame class.  OPEN PARAMETER.
locked.note: The single most consequential constant in the generation-dispatch model.  Every ramp-credit figure shown in the Generation panel is a product of this value and the available dt_lead.  Until measured, all derived ramp-capability numbers are unvalidated.  Claim discipline: do not quote ramp figures externally before replacing this with OEM data.

locked.label: Cold-start time to synchronised
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 900 s (15 min) implied by TC-80 scenario structure.  No OEM basis; frame-class gas turbines typically require 10–30 min from cold to synchronised, depending on turbine model and grid code.  Replace with manufacturer commissioning data.
locked.note: Time from OFFLINE to SYNCHRONISED when the turbine has been offline longer than warm_threshold_s.  Governs commitment timing after a decommit event followed by a cold soak.

locked.label: Warm-start time to synchronised
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 600 s (10 min).  Raised from 300 s (where it was equal to hot_start_s) to restore a meaningful thermal-state distinction.  D-08 fixed hot_start_s at 300 s (frame machines cannot sync in 1 min); landing warm_start_s at the same value made the WARM classification decorative.  600 s (10 min) is physically defensible for a machine that has cooled 1–4 hours: less heat soak than cold (900 s) but more than a machine that has been off < 1 h (hot, 300 s).  No OEM calibration on file; replace with OEM thermal soak curve data.  Cross-parameter invariant: hot_start_s (300) < warm_start_s (600) < cold_start_s (900).
locked.note: Time from OFFLINE to SYNCHRONISED when hot_threshold_s < elapsed ≤ warm_threshold_s.  Must satisfy: warm_start_s < cold_start_s (warm starts faster than cold) and hot_start_s < warm_start_s.  Cross-parameter candidate (not yet enforced as test invariant).

locked.label: Hot-start time to synchronised
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 300 s (5 min).  Corrected from 60 s during Phase D (D-08): a frame-class machine cannot synchronise in one minute.  60 s was an unrealistic bypass value.  300 s kept here; warm_start_s was raised to 600 s to restore a meaningful thermal gap (Item 1 correction).  No OEM basis; replace with manufacturer data for the installed frame class.
locked.note: Time from OFFLINE to SYNCHRONISED when elapsed ≤ hot_threshold_s.  Must satisfy: hot_start_s < warm_start_s ≤ cold_start_s.  Cross-parameter candidate (not yet enforced as test invariant).

locked.label: Combined inertia constant H
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 4.0 s, typical medium diesel/gas island plant.  No measured basis; calibrate against design partner generator specs and system-study data.  OPEN PARAMETER.
locked.note: H sets the entire frequency-response timescale.  The electromechanical time constant is ≈2H/droop, so every derived frequency criterion — trip threshold crossing time, droop settle time, stability margin — scales directly with this value.  Claim discipline: do not quote absolute frequency figures externally until H is measured.

locked.label: Governor droop (per-unit)
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.04 pu (4 %), typical gas turbine governor setting.  No measured basis.  OPEN PARAMETER.
locked.note: Per-unit frequency deviation that produces 100 % governor response.  Governs frequency response alongside inertia_constant_s.  Cross-parameter candidate: 2H/droop gives the electromechanical time constant; both must be measured together.

locked.label: Hot-start thermal threshold
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 3 600 s (1 h).  No OEM calibration.  Turbines offline ≤ this many seconds since last synchronisation are classified as HOT and use hot_start_s.  Replace with OEM thermal cooling-curve data.
locked.note: Ordering invariant candidate: hot_threshold_s < warm_threshold_s (not yet enforced).

locked.label: Warm-start thermal threshold
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 14 400 s (4 h).  No OEM calibration.  Turbines offline > hot_threshold_s and ≤ this use warm_start_s.  Above warm_threshold_s the turbine is COLD.  Replace with OEM thermal cooling-curve data.
locked.note: Ordering invariant candidate: hot_threshold_s < warm_threshold_s (not yet enforced).

locked.label: Levelled-off output tolerance
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.05 MW (50 kW).  PROTO-23.  Must be < r_asset_mw_per_s × dt_seconds (1.0 MW at r=0.2, dt=5) so the predicate does not fire prematurely mid-descent.  No measured basis.
locked.note: Absolute output tolerance (MW) used to detect that an UNLOADING unit has reached its MSL setpoint.  When |output − msl| < tol the levelled_off predicate is True and the unload_tail_s dwell clock starts.  Cross-parameter constraint: must be < r_asset_mw_per_s × dt_seconds.

locked.label: Workload signal staleness threshold
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 30 s.  No measured basis.  A WorkloadSignal is marked stale when none has arrived within this window for an active job.  30 s allows for orchestrator heartbeat intervals of up to 15 s with a 2× margin.
locked.note: Governs the stale-signal alert surfaced in TickResult.  Too short → false alerts under normal orchestrator jitter.  Too long → delayed detection of a silent job exit.

locked.label: BESS first-order response time constant
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.05 s (50 ms), grid-forming inverter class.  No measured basis; calibrate against design partner inverter specs.  OPEN PARAMETER.
locked.note: First-order lag time constant for BESS power delivery: alpha = 1 − exp(−dt/tau).  Representative values: grid-forming VSM 20–50 ms, grid-following PLL 50–150 ms, slow droop UPS 200–500 ms.  Effect on coverage: shorter tau → faster delivery → higher coverage ratio.  Claim discipline: BESS coverage figures are unvalidated until tau is measured.

locked.label: BESS anchor mode
locked.provenance_detail: DR-2026-08-08-FREQ — virtual synchronous machine mode. Grid-forming BESS contributes virtual inertia (vsm_inertia_constant_s) when zero synchronous machines are on-bus.

locked.label: VSM virtual inertia constant
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 2.0 s. No measured basis. Applies when anchor_mode = 'vsm' and zero synchronous machines are on-bus. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: Swing equation sub-step size
locked.provenance_detail: DR-2026-08-08-FREQ — 0.01 s (10 ms). Required for nadir resolution. Must satisfy: dynamic_step_s <= shortest_protection_delay / 10 = 0.015 s.

locked.label: Fixed-speed cooling motor fraction
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 0.30. Fraction of cooling load served by fixed-speed motors (not VFD). These motors produce load damping proportional to speed. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: Motor damping coefficient
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 2.5 pu/pu. Affinity law basis. D_eff = (p_cooling/p_demand) x fixed_speed_cooling_fraction x d_motor ~0.13 at nominal operating point. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: Governor valve actuation time constant
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 0.2 s. No measured basis. First-order lag from governor signal to valve gate position. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: Fuel-to-power time constant
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 1.0 s. No measured basis. First-order lag from fuel valve position to shaft mechanical power output. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: Maximum instantaneous governor load step
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 2.25 MW per sub-step. No measured basis. Bounds the governor output change per dynamic_step_s integration step. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: UFLS stage definitions
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 3 stages. No measured basis. Thresholds and delays must be confirmed against site relay coordination study. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: 81U relay under-frequency trip threshold (islanded)
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 57.5 Hz. No measured basis for islanded operation. NOTE: island_collapse_hz (IEEE 1547 Cat I = 57.0 Hz) is for grid-connected DER interconnection and must not be used as the islanded protection threshold. This PROVISIONAL value replaces it for islanded mode. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: 81U relay clearing delay
locked.provenance_detail: PROVISIONAL-UNMEASURED — 0.10 s (100 ms). No measured basis. Time from threshold crossing to generator trip. Blocks demo export until measured.

locked.label: Per-unit governor droop (per turbine)
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.04 pu/pu. Per-unit alias of governor_droop, used as the default for TurbineConfig.droop_r (Phase 2B per-unit governor). Same value as fleet-level governor_droop.

locked.label: Per-unit turbine power factor default
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.85. Default per-unit power factor for TurbineConfig (Phase 2B). Used to compute per-unit MVA base: S_i = rated_mw_i / power_factor_i. Matches SiteConfig.power_factor default.

locked.label: Governor deadband
locked.provenance_detail: CHOSEN — 0.02 Hz. Was a class-level literal (_GOVERNOR_DEADBAND_HZ) in simulation_core.py. Promoted to catalogue by Phase 1 (DR-2026-08-09-BALANCE) so the value has one authoritative home. No measured basis; typical gas-turbine governor setting.

locked.label: Maximum frequency error for droop clamping (DR-BAL-1 — now derived, not set here)
locked.provenance_detail: DR-BAL-1 CLOSED (C-4). This key is no longer read by simulation_core.py. The Δf clamp is now derived at tick time from `max_frequency_error_from_thresholds(site.frequency_nominal_hz, [site.ufls_stage1_hz, site.of_trip_hz])` — the tightest first-stage UF/OF margin. Retained in the catalogue as a documentation record; value null is intentional (the derived value varies by scenario). The unbounded droop fallback branch has been deleted.
locked.reason: DR-BAL-1 closed — clamp is derived from site.ufls_stage1_hz and site.of_trip_hz; no longer a catalogue setting.

locked.label: Power balance identity tolerance (noise floor, DR-BAL-2)
locked.provenance_detail: CALIBRATED — 1.9913e-14 MW. Derived by running `python3 -m core.calibrate reports/NAR-001_residuals.jsonl --invariant I2a`. I2a is `turbine + bess + renewable - p_generation_mw`; structurally identical to the balance identity and known to close on all 869 recorded ticks (880 samples, 179 non-zero). CLI output: max=3.55271e-15 MW, p99=8.88178e-16 MW, p99.9=1.9913e-15 MW, suggested=p99.9 × 10=1.9913e-14 MW. Sanity check: 1.9913e-14 MW is twelve orders of magnitude below the 14.34 MW and 18.05 MW defects it must catch. DR-BAL-2 closed. The previous value of 0.0 was degenerate: calibrated from demo-baseline (11 idle ticks where arithmetic cancels exactly — an absence of evidence, not a measured floor).
locked.reason: DR-BAL-2 closed — calibrated from I2a over NAR-001_residuals.jsonl (880 ticks).

locked.label: BESS marginal dispatch cost (cycle amortisation method)
locked.provenance_detail: PSP-6 resolved. Methodology: Method A — cycle amortisation. Formula: (battery_capex_per_mwh / cycle_life_cycles) + round_trip_loss_cost_mwh. Component breakdown: (1) Cycle degradation = $125,000/MWh ÷ 5,000 cycles = $25.00/MWh. Source: Ember Oct 2025 assessment, $125/kWh all-in LFP project capex = $125,000/MWh capacity. (2) Round-trip loss cost = 12.5% average loss × $114.82/MWh summer off-peak reference = ~$14.35/MWh charging cost transported to output. Rounded midpoint: $25 + $13 = $38/MWh. This figure covers degradation and round-trip loss only — charging energy cost is NOT included here (would double-count against whatever source charges the battery). Tags both source parameters PROPOSED_HERE per §7; get explicit sign-off before Phase 3 wires BudgetGate. PSP-6 resolved 2026-08-13.
locked.note: Method A: (battery_capex_per_mwh / cycle_life_cycles) + round_trip_loss. Sourced from Lazard LCOS v10.0 and Ember Oct 2025 public references. Requires explicit sign-off before BudgetGate wiring (Phase 3). PSP-6 resolved.

locked.label: BESS all-in capital cost per MWh of usable capacity
locked.provenance_detail: PROPOSED_HERE — $125,000/MWh = $125/kWh. Source: Ember Energy Oct 2025 assessment of degradation/capex-driven BESS cost, utility-scale LFP (lithium iron phosphate) four-hour duration systems. This is an all-in project capex figure including balance-of-plant, EPC, and interconnection but excluding charging energy cost. Lazard LCOS v10.0 (2025) gives $115–$254/MWh unsubsidized for 100MW/4-hour systems (that figure bundles charging energy cost; using Ember's capex-only basis to avoid double-counting). Replace with the actual signed equipment/EPC contract before production deployment. Used in bess_marginal_cost_mwh via Method A formula. PSP-6 resolved 2026-08-13.
locked.note: All-in capex per MWh of usable storage capacity. Source: Ember Oct 2025 ($125/kWh LFP). Used in bess_marginal_cost_mwh = capex/cycles + loss. PSP-6 resolved.

locked.label: BESS useful cycle life (LFP conservative estimate)
locked.provenance_detail: PROPOSED_HERE — 5,000 full discharge cycles. Source: conservative LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cycle-life figure from Ember Oct 2025 assessment and NREL battery storage reference data. LFP chemistry typically delivers 4,000–6,000 cycles at 80% depth of discharge to 80% retained capacity; 5,000 is a mid-range conservative figure. NMC chemistry would be ~1,500–3,000 cycles (higher capex amortisation). Replace with the specific cell chemistry and warranted cycle count from the battery vendor before production deployment. Used in bess_marginal_cost_mwh via Method A formula. PSP-6 resolved 2026-08-13.
locked.note: Conservative LFP cycle life. Used in bess_marginal_cost_mwh = capex/cycles + loss. PSP-6 resolved.

locked.label: PG&E B-20 voltage service class (secondary / primary / transmission)
locked.provenance_detail: PROPOSED_HERE — 'secondary' is the B-20 default and is correct for behind-the-meter systems served at distribution voltage (typically <1kV). A 5–50MW data-centre site may qualify for primary voltage service (1–50kV) or transmission service (>50kV), where B-20 demand charges and energy rates differ materially (transmission demand winter peak: $2.97/kW vs. secondary $2.32/kW). This is a per-deployment parameter — supply the correct voltage class from the signed utility service agreement before production use. Voltage class does not affect energy rates in the current TOU implementation (energy rates are identical across secondary/primary/transmission on Cal. PUC 61081-E), but affects demand charge calculation (out of scope for Phase 1–5). Raised as a design-time gap by Phase 0 review, 2026-08-13.
locked.spec_ref: GS-IMPL-PSP-002 §7 / PG&E B-20 / Cal. PUC Sheet 61081-E (eff. 2026-03-01)
locked.note: Per-deployment. Energy rates on Cal. PUC 61081-E are class-independent for TOU energy component; demand charges are class-dependent and out of scope for Phase 1–5. Set to actual service class from utility agreement before design-partner use.

excluded.reason: Derived from PARAM-20. Exposing it as a free field decouples the hardware profile library from the forecast and silently disables the §5.1 unmapped-hardware path. The profile dropdown is the kW control.
Modelling GPU utilization — the reactive signal the product is positioned against. The legitimate dynamic is the Δt_lead ramp shape from 0 to full TDP, which is a separate mechanism.
Established during the build and protected as regression surface.

invariants.statement: PUE_base and alpha(t) are mutually exclusive overhead buckets.
The reserve check evaluates the confidence band, never the point estimate.
The reserve check uses the anchor-adjusted bridging figure whenever the BESS is grid-forming.
P_renewable reduces load and never contributes to ramp capability.
BESS shortfall declines linearly; never modelled as a flat draw.
A duration is never compared against an energy-like quantity.
A parameter change mid-run is recorded as a scenario event, not a silent mutation. A run must be reproducible from its inputs.
No model inference in the control path.
Superposition is per job instance, not per hardware profile.
NetworkTelemetry is dispatch-path ineligible by contract.

worked_example.note: The 8% band is illustrative only. v2.5 §12 requires a band but does not fix its magnitude — see PARAM-13 and OI-2.

open_items.OI-1: P_anchor_reserve is a property of the island's dynamic stability study, not the battery nameplate. The 8% default is a placeholder pending a commissioning value.
open_items.OI-2: Confidence band magnitudes (PARAM-13/14/15) are unspecified in v2.5. Needs a decision, not a default.
open_items.OI-3: No subscription-semantics table for WorkloadSignal parallel to §25.4's for NetworkTelemetry. Watch vs poll-with-interval vs push is undeclared per source.
open_items.OI-4: Node-label to hardware_profile_id convention is unspecified. This is the field the real adapter must derive and the simulator supplies literally, so the §5.1 fallback is currently unreachable except by deliberate injection.
open_items.OI-5: Genset-anchor droop dynamics are outside the §7 ramp model (PX-2).
open_items.OI-6: f(SOC) — how state of charge derates bridging capability — is asserted but never given a form.
